PROTEST VS CORRUPTION

Pro-democracy groups hold a mass and protest action at the EDSA Shrine in Quezon City on Thursday, September 11, to denounce corruption in government.

The groups, including Tindig Pilipinas, Nagkaisa Labor Coalition, Kalipunan ng Kilusang Masa, and SIKLAB (Simbahan at Komunidad Laban sa Katiwalian), call for the immediate creation of an independent commission to investigate irregularities and demand that all elected officials, particularly those implicated in flood control controversies, release their Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs).

They say the scandals not only involve massive misuse of public funds but also aggravate flooding problems faced by communities. | via Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News

‘𝗣𝘂𝗻𝗶𝘀𝗵 𝗔𝗹𝗹 𝗣𝗹𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗿𝘀’: 𝗔𝗸𝗯𝗮𝘆𝗮𝗻 𝘀𝗮𝘆𝘀 𝗙𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗱 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹 𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗺 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲𝘀 𝗗𝗲𝗲𝗽 𝗣𝗼𝗹𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗘𝗽𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗺𝗶𝗰

Hundreds of citizens led by Akbayan Partylist, Tindig Pilipinas, and Youth Against Kurakot (YaK!) converged at the historic EDSA Shrine today in a mass celebration and protest action to denounce the trillion-peso flood control scandal that siphoned away people’s money meant for vital infrastructure.

Akbayan underscored that the massive corruption in flood control projects is not an isolated scam but a symptom of a larger, systemic political epidemic.

Deputy Minority Leader Akbayan Rep. Perci Cendaña condemned the gravity of the scandal, likening it to a new epidemic afflicting the nation. “May nakakatakot na bagong epidemya ang umuusbong ngayon—ang sakit na Kleptospirosis. Imbes katawan, kaban ng bayan ang pinupuntirya,” Cendaña warned.

Read more: https://t.co/08dC7NmDo8

#AkbayanPartylist

LOOK: Department of the Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, together with PLDT Chairman and CEO Manny Pangilinan, Next Generation Advanced Technology 911 Co-Founder and CEO Don Ferguson and Mike Amos, Philippine National Police Chief PLTGEN Jose Melencio Nartatez, and Bureau of Fire Protection Chief Fire Director Jesus Piedad Fernandez, officially launch the Unified 911 emergency response system at the PLDT Office along España Street in Manila City on Thursday, September 11.

The Unified 911 program, designed to be language-sensitive—with support for Tagalog, Cebuano, Ilocano, Waray, Tausug, and other Philippine languages—aims to provide nationwide emergency services through the PNP, BFP, and other medical responders. 

📸: Santi San Juan/MB
